correctness.rationale: For fixed \(0\le r<m\le n\) with \(d=m-r\ge2\), the joint law of all risk-normalized spacings is an explicit hypoexponential first spacing and remaining independent exponential gaps. The CDF follows by comparing independent positive sums and the exact distinct-rate survival partial fractions. The lower tail is an exact one-negative-summand product; the upper tail is a dominated small-ball simplex expansion, with the full symmetric-polynomial moment coefficient. Coupling the first spacing with its final exponential term proves strict stochastic shift. A standard-library checker passed 413 exact rational and direct censoring-simulation checks. Finite checks do not substitute for the proof.

value.rationale: Qin–Yu–Gui explicitly sought a finite-null calibration of a natural censored exponentiality test but used approximations. The elementary, all-parameter rational CDF gives exact finite-sample critical values; the sharp left/right tail exponents show that initial unobserved failures create a structural asymmetry relevant to extreme two-sided thresholds; strict stochastic comparison quantifies the null shift. This is not merely a recoding of a normalization check or arbitrary narrow numerical slice.
